# Writing `docs/` Pages

`docs/` is a MyST site (`docs/myst.yml`, book-theme). Every page is about Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, so don't
add scope banners saying that.

## Core rules

1. **Prefer MyST syntax over plain Markdown** when MyST has an equivalent. For example, use a
   ` ```{list-table} ` instead of a pipe table and `{note}` instead of a bold "Note:" line.
2. **Use a compact visual form whenever the information allows it.** If content has a repeated shape (values
   per item, options with pros and cons, per-character behavior), make it a table. Use prose only for
   explanation that doesn't fit a grid.
3. **Document every external source the standard way**: a collapsed Sources dropdown at the end of the page,
   plus `% research:` comments right below it. See [Sources](#sources-required-standard). This applies
   whenever a page gains or changes information that came from outside (wiki, Discord, Twitter/X, video,
   spreadsheet, another player's lab).

## Choosing a format

| Content shape | Use |
|---|---|
| Items × attributes (moves, characters, stages, options) | `list-table` with `:header-rows: 1` |
| Key → value facts (a "snapshot" of a character or mechanic) | 2-column `list-table` with no header row, bold keys |
| A formula, multiplier, or number per state or condition | `list-table` (State / Value / Notes) |
| Ordered steps (inputs, labbing setup) | Numbered list |
| Short standalone facts | Bulleted list, one fact per bullet, key term in **bold** |
| Optional depth, definitions, long caveats | `:::{dropdown}` |
| Must-know callout | `{note}` / `{tip}` / `{warning}` admonition, used sparingly |
| Side-by-side media or summaries | `::::{grid}` + `:::{card}` |
| Math | `$...$` inline or `{math}` block |

(The table above is a pipe table on purpose, since skill files aren't rendered by MyST.)

## MyST patterns used in this repo

**List table.** This is the default for any table. Wrap numbers, percents and move inputs in backticks, as
existing pages do (eg `` `62%-116%` ``). Give a table a `:label:` when other text links to it.

````markdown
```{list-table}
:header-rows: 1
:label: stale-reductors

* - Queue position
  - Reductor
* - `1`
  - `0.09`
```
````

**Snapshot (key → value, no header).** See `docs/matchups/bowser.md`.

````markdown
```{list-table}
* - **Size**
  - `Super Heavyweight`
```
````

**Dropdown.** Use a dropdown for detail most readers can skip. To nest a directive inside, use 4 colons on the
outer fence.

```markdown
:::{dropdown} Definitions
...
:::
```

**Labels and cross-references:** put `(my-label)=` on the line before a heading, then link it with
`[](#my-label)` or `[text](#my-label)`.

**Comments and TODOs:** use `% TODO: ...` lines. MyST doesn't render them. Don't put them above the
frontmatter, because frontmatter must be the very first thing in the file.

**Frontmatter:** use only MyST-valid keys: `title`, `description`, `keywords`, `tags`. List community
synonyms and shorthand in `keywords` so search (human and AI) finds the page. Put the generated-file
attribution comment right after the frontmatter.

## Page structure

- **Start with a `## Summary`** of short bullets, or a snapshot table, that answers most questions. Details go
  in the sections below it.
- **Make each section self-contained.** Name the move, character or mechanic instead of writing "it", so a
  section still makes sense when read on its own.
- **Put your own interpretation under its own labeled heading** (eg `## Practical takeaways`), separate from
  sourced facts. Mark computed numbers as *Derived*.
- **End with the Sources dropdown and `% research:` comments** (see below).
- **Glossary:** when a page introduces a term, alias or shorthand, add a row to `docs/glossary.md` (Term /
  Also called / Meaning / See) linking back to the page. AI search expands questions through this table.
- **Placement:** engine mechanics go in `docs/mechanics/`, matchups in `docs/matchups/<character>.md`, and
  Little Mac tech in `docs/tech.md`. `docs/scratch/**` is excluded from the site build.

## Sources (required standard)

Every page that uses external information ends with this block. It must be the last thing on the page, with
no `## Sources` heading and no sources scattered elsewhere as a "Sources" list.

```markdown
:::{dropdown} Sources
- [SmashWiki: Stale Moves](https://www.ssbwiki.com/Stale_Moves) — pulled 2026-09-29
- Shield staling at `0.85×`: [Meshima datamine](https://twitter.com/Meshima_/status/1078340842169950208)
  (cited by the wiki; not re-verified)
:::

% research: ssbwiki Stale_Moves revid=2039011 pulled=2026-09-29
% research: staged: local/staging/wiki/2026-09-29_ssbwiki_stale-moves.md (machine-local)
% research: kept "Brawl onward"/"Smash 4 onward"/Ultimate sections; dropped 64/Melee/Brawl specifics
% research: knockback 30% rule inherited from SSB4 section
% research: unverified: shield 0.85x (single datamine)
```

**Dropdown (for people, rendered collapsed):** one bullet per source, with a descriptive link text and the
pull date.
- If a single claim rests on its own source, name the claim first (`Claim: [source](url)`).
- Mark anything that hasn't been independently verified.
- For your own lab results, use `Lab: <what was tested> — <date>`.

**`% research:` lines (for AI, never rendered):** one fact per line, always starting with `% research:` so
they're greppable. Record the following:

| What | Example |
|---|---|
| Source version | `ssbwiki Stale_Moves revid=2039011 pulled=2026-09-29` |
| Staged raw copy (one line per file, directly under its source's line) | `staged: local/staging/wiki/2026-09-29_ssbwiki_stale-moves.md (machine-local)` |
| Non-versioned source | `discord #mac-labs author=<name> date=2026-09-01 link=<message url>` |
| Scope kept / dropped | `dropped Melee/Brawl specifics, controversy` |
| Inherited behavior | `knockback rule inherited from SSB4 ("generally unchanged")` |
| Resolved conflicts | `items: Ultimate section overrides general section` |
| Unverified claims | `unverified: shield 0.85x` |
| Lab setup | `lab: vs Mario 0%, stale moves OFF, no DI, 2026-09-30` |

**When editing an existing page:**
- **Adding sourced info:** add the new source to the dropdown and add `% research:` lines. Update an existing
  line instead of duplicating it, eg a new `revid`/`pulled` after a re-pull.
- **Old-style sources:** if the page has an old-style `## Sources` section or loose source list and you're
  adding sources anyway, convert it to this standard.
- **Inline links:** links used as content (eg a video in a tech table) stay where they are.

## Before finishing a page

- [ ] Frontmatter is first in the file, uses only MyST-valid keys, and `keywords` lists synonyms.
- [ ] Tables are `list-table`, and repeated-shape info is in a table rather than prose.
- [ ] `## Summary` is at the top, and interpretations are labeled.
- [ ] External info has a Sources dropdown plus `% research:` lines at the very end of the page.
- [ ] New terms and aliases are in `docs/glossary.md`.
